title: Negating leaves negates the evaluation
statement: Let $T$ be a decision tree on $n$ Boolean variables, and let $x \colon \{0,\dots,n-1\} \to \{\mathtt{false},\mathtt{true}\}$ be an assignment of the variables. Then the tree obtained from $T$ by negating every leaf value evaluates on $x$ to the negation of the value of $T$ on $x$; that is, its output equals $\lnot\,(T(x))$.
hypotheses_covered: T is a decision tree on n Boolean variables
x is an assignment Fin n → Bool
